dossier.public_summary: The 13.5-day dips are not consistent. Odd-numbered transits are ~600-1400 ppm deep while even transits are near zero, and individual transits vary from very deep to no dip at all. The signal is driven by a few deep events, not a steady planet transit. The pattern matches an eclipsing binary seen at twice the claimed period, not a planet.

reasons.why: Odd and even transits differ by ~8.8 sigma, depth_difference 1.004 (605.8 ppm). Even events are near zero/noise, odd events are deep. This is positive evidence for a binary at twice the period (P=27 d), not a planet.

Depth is not steady even within SPOC 2-min: sector depths 1289, 413, 77, 1384, -22, 213 ppm, depth_change_pct 251.5. Coherent 13.5 d planet would be steady; this alternation matches alternating primary and secondary eclipses of an EB at twice the period.

Signal is carried by 2-3 deep odd events; many individual transits are consistent with zero depth. A planet produces consistent dips; episodic deep dips + nulls indicate false alarm / diluted EB, not a planet.
reasons.value: p_consistent 1.1783562464539717e-43, share_of_top_3 0.945, outliers depth 1384 ppm sigma 8.9, 1289 ppm sigma 7.9

reasons.why: Planet size and no plausible neighbour support planet, but centroid is inconclusive and does not rule out on-target EB, which remains the best explanation given odd/even and depth variability.
